container_info.description:
This project aims to automate the process of connecting to public GitHub repositories, ingesting their codebases, and generating comprehensive documentation for the ingested code. The system will streamline code understanding, onboarding, and maintenance by providing clear, structured, and up-to-date documentation derived directly from source code. The project is intended for developers, technical writers, and organizations seeking to improve codebase transparency and reduce manual documentation effort.

Key outcomes include automated code parsing, documentation generation, and integration with GitHub APIs, ensuring scalability and adaptability for various programming languages and repository structures.
container_info.reasoning: The project is a server-side system that connects to GitHub, ingests code repositories, and generates documentation — clearly a backend/API service. The container already includes Python 3, uvicorn, requests, beautifulsoup4, sphinx and mkdocs, and dotnet and Node tooling; however Python tooling and uvicorn are present and well-suited for building RESTful APIs and async IO required for repository ingestion. FastAPI provides a lightweight, high-performance async web framework that works well with uvicorn, is minimal for headless containers, and integrates easily with background workers (Celery is present) and documentation generation tools (Sphinx/MkDocs).
requirements: minimal dependency for GitHub integration: pip install requests PyGithub
parser/analysis libs as needed: pip install pygments astor (or language-specific parsers as required)
documentation tooling (already present): sphinx and/or mkdocs; install mkdocs-material only if necessary
background task runner if asynchronous jobs needed: celery and redis (redis-server present) — install celery
basic lightweight DB for metadata: sqlite3 (builtin) or use file storage; avoid PostgreSQL/MySQL unless required
basic test: pytest (install pytest) for minimal validation
run server with uvicorn in development: uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
minimal environment variables for headless operation: GITHUB_TOKEN (optional for rate limits), WORKDIR path, and LOG_LEVEL=INFO
avoid production components: do not install Gunicorn, complex monitoring agents, or enterprise DB drivers in minimal setup

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Create an idempotent /etc/profile.d file that persistently sets WORKDIR and LOG_LEVEL as literal values (no runtime expansion). Perform a lightweight preflight to verify python, pip, uvicorn, and celery are present and print their versions for visibility. Do not write GITHUB_TOKEN; callers must provide it at runtime. The script uses a single-quoted heredoc to avoid variable expansion when writing the profile, installs the profile atomically only if changed, sources it for this run with a local fallback, and avoids unnecessary apt operations when tools are already available.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/test-project-ajay-8050-8164/API&Services(Backend)"
PROFILE_FILE="/etc/profile.d/api_services_backend.sh"
TMPFILE=$(mktemp)
# Use single-quoted heredoc so variables are not expanded into the file
cat >"${TMPFILE}" <<'EOF'
# API&Services(Backend) environment - autogenerated
# WARNING: do NOT write secrets here (GITHUB_TOKEN must be supplied at runtime)
export WORKDIR='/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/test-project-ajay-8050-8164/API&Services(Backend)'
export LOG_LEVEL='INFO'
EOF
# Atomically install only if different
if ! sudo test -f "${PROFILE_FILE}" || ! sudo cmp -s "${TMPFILE}" "${PROFILE_FILE}"; then
  sudo install -m 0644 "${TMPFILE}" "${PROFILE_FILE}"
fi
rm -f "${TMPFILE}"
# Source for this script; if that fails, fall back to literal
if sudo test -r "${PROFILE_FILE}"; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source "${PROFILE_FILE}" || true
fi
: "${WORKDIR:=${WORKSPACE}}"
# Preflight: verify presence and versions of key tools (do not reinstall)
if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: python3 not found" >&2; exit 2
fi
python3 --version || true
if command -v python3 -m pip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 -m pip --version || true
fi
# Check uvicorn and celery (preinstalled in image). Print versions if available
if command -v uvicorn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  uvicorn --version 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if command -v celery >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  celery --version 2>/dev/null || true
fi

steps.name: scaffolding
steps.description: Create a minimal FastAPI project structure under the authoritative workspace, a requirements.txt with the minimal dependency list, and generate a resilient start.sh that derives WORKDIR from the environment with a single authoritative default injected once at generation time. Files are created only if absent to preserve idempotency.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/test-project-ajay-8050-8164/API&Services(Backend)"
mkdir -p "${WORKSPACE}" && cd "${WORKSPACE}"
# Minimal FastAPI app
if [ ! -f "${WORKSPACE}/app/main.py" ]; then
  mkdir -p "${WORKSPACE}/app"
  cat > "${WORKSPACE}/app/main.py" <<'PY'
from fastapi import FastAPI
app = FastAPI()

@app.get('/health')
def health():
    return {'status': 'ok'}

@app.get('/')
def root():
    return {'message': 'Hello from FastAPI'}
PY
fi
# requirements (create only if missing)
REQ_FILE="${WORKSPACE}/requirements.txt"
if [ ! -f "${REQ_FILE}" ]; then
  cat > "${REQ_FILE}" <<'REQ'
fastapi
uvicorn[standard]
requests
PyGithub
pygments
astor
celery
pytest
REQ
fi
# start.sh: derive WORKDIR from env or default to single authoritative path (injected once)
START_SH="${WORKSPACE}/start.sh"
if [ ! -f "${START_SH}" ]; then
  cat > "${START_SH}" <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# If WORKDIR is provided in the environment use it, otherwise default to injected path
WORKDIR="${WORKSPACE}"
WORKDIR="${WORKDIR:-${WORKSPACE}}"
export WORKDIR
cd "${WORKDIR}"
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
# Activate venv if present
if [ -f "${WORKDIR}/.venv/bin/activate" ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  source "${WORKDIR}/.venv/bin/activate"
fi
LOG_LEVEL_ARG="--log-level ${LOG_LEVEL:-info}"
exec uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 ${LOG_LEVEL_ARG}
SH
  chmod +x "${START_SH}"
fi

steps.name: dependencies
steps.description: Create or reuse a workspace-local virtualenv (.venv), validate python and pip versions (fail-fast if missing or too old), install missing packages from requirements.txt into the venv, and verify imports with reasonable fallbacks. Skip complex VCS/editable requirement lines and log them for operator awareness. Warn if preinstalled uvicorn/celery versions appear older than a recommended baseline.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/test-project-ajay-8050-8164/API&Services(Backend)"
cd "${WORKSPACE}"
REQ_FILE="${WORKSPACE}/requirements.txt"
# Basic version checks
if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: python3 not found" >&2; exit 2
fi
PYVER=$(python3 -c 'import sys; print(".".join(map(str,sys.version_info[:2])))') || true
# Require at least Python 3.11 as a soft baseline (adjustable)
MIN_PY_MAJOR=3; MIN_PY_MINOR=11
PY_MAJOR=$(python3 -c 'import sys;print(sys.version_info[0])')
PY_MINOR=$(python3 -c 'import sys;print(sys.version_info[1])')
if [ "${PY_MAJOR}" -lt "${MIN_PY_MAJOR}" ] || { [ "${PY_MAJOR}" -eq "${MIN_PY_MAJOR}" ] && [ "${PY_MINOR}" -lt "${MIN_PY_MINOR}" ]; }; then
  echo "WARNING: python version ${PYVER} is older than recommended ${MIN_PY_MAJOR}.${MIN_PY_MINOR}" >&2
fi
# Create venv if missing
if [ ! -d "${WORKSPACE}/.venv" ]; then
  python3 -m venv "${WORKSPACE}/.venv"
fi
# Activate venv
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "${WORKSPACE}/.venv/bin/activate"
# Ensure pip is available and recent
python -m pip --version || (python -m pip install --upgrade pip && python -m pip --version)
# Warn about preinstalled uvicorn/celery versions on system PATH
if command -v uvicorn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  uvicorn --version 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if command -v celery >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  celery --version 2>/dev/null || true
fi
# Build a mapping of expected import names (extendable)
declare -A IMPORT_MAP=( [fastapi]=fastapi [uvicorn]=uvicorn [requests]=requests [pygithub]=github [pygments]=pygments [astor]=astor [celery]=celery [pytest]=pytest )
TO_INSTALL=()
SKIP_LINES=()
# Read requirements, skip empty/comments, skip VCS/editable lines and note them
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "${line}" ]; do
  raw=$(echo "${line}" | sed -e 's/^\s*//;s/\s*$//')
  [ -z "${raw}" ] && continue
  case "${raw}" in
    \#*) continue ;;
    -e*|git+*|http:*|https:*) SKIP_LINES+=("${raw}"); continue ;;
  esac
  base=$(echo "${raw}" | sed -E 's/([^\[=<>!~]+).*/\1/' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
  import_name="${IMPORT_MAP[${base}]:-${base}}"
  # Try import; if missing, schedule install
  if ! python - <<PY
import importlib.util,sys
if importlib.util.find_spec('${import_name}') is None:
    sys.exit(1)
else:
    sys.exit(0)
PY
  then
    TO_INSTALL+=("${raw}")
  fi
done < "${REQ_FILE}"
if [ ${#SKIP_LINES[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  printf '%s
' "SKIPPED complex requirement lines:" "${SKIP_LINES[@]}" >&2
fi
# Install missing packages
if [ ${#TO_INSTALL[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
  python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check "${TO_INSTALL[@]}"
fi
# Verification pass with logging of any missing import fallbacks
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "${line}" ]; do
  raw=$(echo "${line}" | sed -e 's/^\s*//;s/\s*$//')
  [ -z "${raw}" ] && continue
  case "${raw}" in
    \#*) continue ;;
    -e*|git+*|http:*|https:*) continue ;;
  esac
  base=$(echo "${raw}" | sed -E 's/([^\[=<>!~]+).*/\1/' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
  import_name="${IMPORT_MAP[${base}]:-${base}}"
  if ! python - <<PY
import importlib.util,sys
if importlib.util.find_spec('${import_name}') is None:
    sys.exit(1)
else:
    sys.exit(0)
PY
  then
    echo "Dependency verification failed for ${raw} (tried import '${import_name}')" >&2
    exit 3
  fi
done < "${REQ_FILE}"
# Print pip version as final verification
python -m pip --version

steps.name: testing
steps.description: Create a minimal pytest test that uses FastAPI's TestClient to exercise /health, run pytest inside the venv and capture full output to tests/pytest.log. Return pytest's exit code to the caller. This provides deterministic evidence for automated validation.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/test-project-ajay-8050-8164/API&Services(Backend)"
cd "${WORKSPACE}"
# Activate venv
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "${WORKSPACE}/.venv/bin/activate"
mkdir -p tests
cat > tests/test_health.py <<'PY'
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
client = TestClient(app)

def test_health():
    r = client.get('/health')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.json().get('status') == 'ok'
PY
# Run pytest, capture stdout+stderr to log and preserve exit code
pytest --maxfail=1 2>&1 | tee tests/pytest.log
EXIT_CODE=${PIPESTATUS[0]:-0}
if [ ${EXIT_CODE} -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "pytest failed (exit ${EXIT_CODE}), see tests/pytest.log" >&2
  exit ${EXIT_CODE}
fi

steps.description: Build (no-op for Python), start the app via start.sh under a process group, wait up to VALIDATION_TIMEOUT seconds (default 60) for /health to respond on 127.0.0.1:8000, return the health response for evidence, and cleanly terminate the process group. On failure print last 200 lines of server log. Verify PID command line before killing to reduce PID-reuse risk.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/test-project-ajay-8050-8164/API&Services(Backend)"
cd "${WORKSPACE}"
START_SH="${WORKSPACE}/start.sh"
if [ ! -x "${START_SH}" ]; then
  echo "start.sh missing or not executable" >&2
  exit 4
fi
LOGFILE=$(mktemp)
export WORKDIR="${WORKSPACE}"
# Start under setsid to create a process group; redirect output to log
setsid "${START_SH}" >"${LOGFILE}" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
# Allow child processes to settle, then capture PGID
sleep 0.5
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= "${PID}" | tr -d ' ')
# helper to check PID command line to avoid killing unrelated processes
pid_matches() {
  if ps -p "${PID}" -o args= 2>/dev/null | grep -q -E 'start.sh|uvicorn|python'; then
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}
cleanup() {
  if [ -n "${PGID}" ]; then
    # only kill if pid still matches expected command
    if pid_matches; then
      kill -TERM -"${PGID}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      sleep 2
      if pid_matches; then
        kill -KILL -"${PGID}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      fi
    fi
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
# Readiness loop (configurable timeout)
VALIDATION_TIMEOUT=${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT:-60}
i=0
while [ $i -lt "${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT}" ]; do
  if curl -sS --fail http://127.0.0.1:8000/health >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 1; i=$((i+1))
done
if [ $i -ge "${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT}" ]; then
  echo "Validation failed: server did not respond within ${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT}s" >&2
  echo "---- server log (last 200 lines) ----" >&2
  tail -n 200 "${LOGFILE}" >&2 || true
  exit 3
fi
# Show evidence
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8000/health || true
# Cleanup (trap will terminate the process group)
cleanup
# Print last part of logs for evidence
tail -n 200 "${LOGFILE}" || true
rm -f "${LOGFILE}"
